Ogden's depot economy and NAS 410: when an SNT-TC-1A certification is enough and when it is not

Ogden's aerospace economy grows out of Hill Air Force Base and the Ogden Air Logistics Complex, one of the Air Force's major depots for fighter aircraft and weapons systems. Around it sit the contractors that support depot work, Williams International's small gas turbine engine plant in Ogden, Northrop Grumman's rocket motor operations in Box Elder County and its Roy campus, and machining and composite shops across Weber and Davis counties. Three questions sort out which document governs your certification: who employs you, who their customer is, and what the contract says.

Inside the fence at Hill

The depot's own NDT workforce operates under Air Force directives and technical orders. Those rules belong to the service, and no civilian course or certification substitutes for them. If you are leaving Air Force maintenance for a civilian NDT job, expect your next employer to examine and certify you again, and carry every training record, experience log and examination result you are allowed to keep.

Contractors and suppliers around the base

Companies that maintain, modify or make parts for military aircraft work to their contracts. Defense aerospace contracts commonly flow NAS 410 down from the prime, a pattern that goes back to 1998, when NAS 410 took over from MIL-STD-410. Under a NAS 410 clause the employer certifies each inspector through a written practice approved by a Responsible Level 3 (RL3), and the prime's auditors and Nadcap's read the personnel files. Some contracts name a service document or a commercial standard instead; the program's Level 3 knows which applies. A contractor's technicians may work on the base under the contractor's own written practice; gate access and NDT certification are separate matters.

Engines and motors on the north side

Turbine engine parts and rocket motor hardware get some of the most demanding inspection in northern Utah: ultrasonic scanning of forgings, fluorescent penetrant on finished surfaces, magnetic particle on steel parts and radiography of cases. Engine and propulsion customers typically write their personnel standard into supplier purchase orders, and for aerospace hardware that is usually NAS 410 or EN 4179. Expect the surface-method gap: NAS 410 asks for more formal, documented penetrant and magnetic particle training than SNT-TC-1A recommends. The magnetic particle testing course and the aviation eddy current guide show what aerospace shops expect.

OTECH, SLCC or online: what an RL3 will look at

Ogden candidates can train in Ogden-Weber Technical College's non-destructive inspection program, at Salt Lake Community College to the south, or online. Whichever you choose, the RL3 of a NAS 410 employer will ask the same things: an approved course outline, the instructor's qualification, recorded hours per method, and supervised experience logged and signed as it was earned. Ask the school, too, whether its practical work uses aerospace parts and procedures or general specimens, because an RL3 will weigh that. A completion certificate alone is weak evidence. An SNT-TC-1A certification held at an earlier employer counts as evidence too, but it does not satisfy a NAS 410 requirement by itself.

For shops in Weber and Davis counties

Write the standard and revision on every certification, plan the update to NAS 410 Revision 6, released in December 2025, and keep industrial and aerospace certifications clearly apart if you serve both. Apply the stricter vision and recertification rule wherever the two schemes differ, so one technician never carries two conflicting records. Atlantis prepares and reviews NAS 410 audit documentation for your RL3's approval ahead of customer and Nadcap AC7114 audits.

Where Atlantis fits for Ogden

Ogden's aerospace and aviation employers can use Atlantis for ASNT NDT Level III consulting, SNT-TC-1A-based training and UT, MT, PT and VT inspection, just as a refinery contractor down the Front can. The training pairs self-paced online theory and ASNT NDT Level III Q&A with practice in the Practical NDT simulator; the hands-on work and the practical examination take place at the employer's facility, and Atlantis has no classroom in Ogden. Atlantis does not provide NAS 410 training, certification, examinations or a Responsible Level 3 to Ogden employers or to contractors at Hill. If you want outside training credited toward a NAS 410 certification, clear it with the employer's RL3 first. The NAS 410 vs SNT-TC-1A comparison and the Salt Lake City page cover the rest of the Front.
